title: Unbounded Concurrency Fanout (Lack of Join Throttle)
pattern: Iterating over a collection of items, mapping them to async tasks spawned directly into the runtime, and executing/joining them concurrently (e.g., using `join_all`) without limiting active task concurrency.
why_bad: Fanning out to perform thousands of concurrent asynchronous tasks can saturate client resources, exhausting socket limits, file descriptors, and local memory [158, 204]. It also floods downstream servers with a "tsunami of requests," degrading network switches and triggering connection backlog drops or timeouts [158, 204].
detection: Mapping an array or iterator of arbitrary length to spawned async tasks or futures that are evaluated concurrently without semaphores or rate limiters.
fix: Control concurrent task execution using an async `Semaphore` or stream concurrency limiters like `.buffer_unordered(limit)` [206].
source: Richard L. Sites, *Understanding Software Dynamics*, Chapter 1.4 (Long-Tail Latency) / passage [158]; Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, Chapter 4 (Unbalanced Capacities) / passages [204, 206].
